images.title: Matchstick triangle row
images.purpose: Show that a row of 5 triangles sharing sides uses 11 matchsticks: 3, then 2 more each time.
images.composition: One strip of 5 triangles centred, with two short labels below.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal strip of 5 triangles sharing sides, alternately pointing up and down, starting and ending pointing up, drawn as 11 straight sticks of equal length: 5 horizontal and 6 slanted. The 3 sticks of the first triangle are teal #0072B2, the other 8 sticks are amber #E69F00. Three labels. Exactly 5 triangles and 11 sticks.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a triangle whose sticks are not equal in length, or a count other than 11 sticks
images.takeaway: Each new triangle adds 2 sticks, so 5 triangles use 11.
images.description: A row of five triangles made of 11 matchsticks, the first triangle teal and the added sticks amber, labelled 5 triangles = 11 sticks.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the amber sticks and say why each triangle adds only 2.

image_decisions.why: Sharing sides is the whole idea, and one strip of sticks shows it.
